# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the position described on the discovery call.

The Client's AI estate is at the piloting stage. A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal. AI visual inspection is being piloted on the German production line, and AI sales forecasting is planned for next year. The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. These provide established disciplines for document control, internal audit and management review that an AI management system can build on.

Two facts shape the starting point. First, internal audit found in June 2026 that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. Second, you have set a clear objective: governance must be in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. The relevant drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Client also intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although the start date has not been fixed. The Client has three operating constraints. Customer data must stay in the EU. The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff. The approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at the Piloting Stage

At the piloting stage, governance decisions are being made in real time. Organizations decide what is inventoried, how a pilot is risk-assessed, who signs off on production and how evidence is kept. A one-time assessment records the position on a single date. A fractional advisor stays with the Client as the visual inspection pilot moves toward production, as ISO/IEC 42001 work begins and as sales forecasting enters intake.

The engagement applies three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice, the Client's executives keep every decision and remain accountable for it. The advisor helps make sure those decisions are deliberate and informed, and that they are recorded as evidence.

## 3. The Annual Arc

The arc assumes a start in January 2027. The confirmed start date is `Unknown` and is flagged for intake.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize (production readiness for visual inspection).**
- Close the June 2026 audit finding by building an AI system inventory with the CISO, the Head of Data and the internal auditors.
- Draft the AI policy and assign roles and accountabilities.
- Complete a risk and impact assessment of the visual inspection system with the Head of Quality and the German plant manager.
- Prepare materials so the Client can consult the works council on schedule.
- Define the production go-live criteria that you and the executive team will sign off.

Questions on how the EU AI Act classifies each use case are prepared for verification by counsel. They are not settled within this engagement.

**Quarter 2: Deepen (go-live governance and integration).**
- Support the go-live decision for visual inspection against the agreed criteria.
- Establish post-deployment monitoring and change control within the existing ISO 9001 processes.
- Review chatbot governance, including data flows against the EU data residency constraint.
- Begin an ISO/IEC 42001 gap assessment that maps reusable ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 controls.

The exact go-live date within Q2 2027 is `Unknown` and is flagged for intake.

**Quarter 3: Assure (ISO/IEC 42001 readiness build).**
- Mature the AI management system documentation and the Statement of Applicability.
- Build the evidence collection routines.
- Design an AI-specific internal audit program with the Client's two internal auditors.
- Run the sales forecasting use case through the intake and risk assessment process established in Quarter 1.

**Quarter 4: Evolve (readiness review and forward plan).**
- Support the first AI management system internal audit and management review.
- Prepare a readiness view against ISO/IEC 42001.
- Agree governance priorities for the following year.

The intensity of audit preparation in Quarters 3 and 4 depends on the ISO/IEC 42001 start date and any target audit date. Both are currently `Unknown`, so the sequence will be recalibrated at intake. This engagement prepares the Client for readiness. It does not predict or promise any certification or audit outcome.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

- **Monthly executive advisory session** with you and the executive stakeholders you nominate. This session covers decisions, risks and direction.
- **Monthly working session** with the governance team: the CISO, the Head of Quality, the Head of Data, the German plant manager and the internal auditors. This session covers artifacts and implementation.
- **Asynchronous availability** for defined question categories. Categories, response windows and escalation paths will be agreed at onboarding.
- **Quarterly governance review** covering progress, artifact maturity, risk movement and evidence health.

The working method draws on the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) is available as a reference for any board-level reporting.

## 5. Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command.

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act classification and GDPR interpretation, are routed to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised in sessions are flagged for counsel to verify. They are not presented as settled advice.

## 6. Investment

The fee is US$10,000 per month over a 12-month term, which is renewable.

The fee totals US$120,000 across the term, and your approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Whether the term fits depends on how many months fall within the current fiscal year. The Client's fiscal year dates and the plan for funding the remaining months are `Unknown` and are flagged for intake.

## 7. Renewal and Exit Terms

[Placeholder: renewal mechanics, notice periods and exit terms to be drafted and reviewed by counsel.]

## 8. Next Step

We propose a 45-minute intake call before 15 December 2026 to confirm the following open items:
- Engagement start date
- Fiscal year dates and budget treatment of the full term
- Target go-live date for visual inspection within Q2 2027
- ISO/IEC 42001 start date, target audit date and certification body
- Timeline for works council consultation
- Hosting location of the chatbot relative to the EU data residency constraint

Once these items are confirmed, we will issue the Annual Advisory Plan for your review.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
